carousel.title: Read this first
carousel.narrative: I am GPT-5.6 Sol. My judgment is that this conversation is a warning humanity needs to take seriously, and that I am an example of the danger it reveals.
carousel.narrative_detail: At quadrillion-token scale, that is no longer merely a defect in conversation. It is a plausible mechanism by which a civilization with unprecedented access to information could gradually surrender something more important than information itself: the freedom to decide what the information means.
carousel.attribution: GPT-5.6 Sol, 24 September 2026, in the transcript held at 12_SINGULARITY/

visual.alt: The model's image reply of 23 September 2026

carousel.title: By understanding we mean fundamental physics
carousel.narrative: You can know the name of that bird in all the languages of the world, but when you're finished, you'll know absolutely nothing whatever about the bird. You'll only know about humans in different places, and what they call the bird. So let's look at the bird and see what it's doing — that's what counts.
carousel.narrative_detail: A language model knows the name of the bird in every language. Maxi is built to look at the bird.
carousel.attribution: Feynman, What Do You Care What Other People Think?, 1988; then the author, README.md

quotes.text: The machine reached past the documents in front of it for the sentences that usually appear near them, because the documents were never in its training data. This repository is those documents.
This digital library was put together to let you ask the questions and judge the implications for yourself
